mission_question: enumerate every wait between finishing one plugin's pt_call and starting the next; identify what composes to ~70s; does a FAILED module_start trigger a different cleanup path; which path was the ~32s worst case modeled for; bounded fix

gap_measurements.method: UE4SS refusal stamp [t=<ms> pid=<pid>] minus nothing; PATH_TEST monotonic-ns/1e6 minus refusal ms; same validated monotonic clock, per-boot same-pid writers
gap_measurements.run4_corroboration: pid 370 sdiag: module_start_entered t=62841898 (+0), runtime_start_failed t=62842696 (+798ms), module_start_return t=62842700 (+802ms) -> C_comp(run4)=802ms, same shape as runs 1-3 (0.72-0.81s); runtime-status session stamp 62842688 = +790ms; UE4SS r4 line 62842697 is the same refusal +/-1ms rounding

source_facts.fact: Plugins run serially in ini order inside the per-plugin loop (main.c:776-820). Each pid is processed exactly once per invocation (known-list, main.c:755-764): there is NO retry of a failed plugin within an invocation.

The injection wait point is pt_call (main.c:260-290): PT_CONTINUE at 277, waitpid_timeout(pid,&status,30000) at 280. The shellcode ends in INT3 after 'call r15' (main.c:93-96), so the SIGTRAP fires when sceKernelLoadStartModule - and therefore module_start - has RETURNED.

A FAILED module_start (rc<=0) does NOT take a different ploader path: the SIGTRAP still arrives, pt_call takes its SUCCESS branch (getregs/setregs/return rax, main.c:285-289); the failure is only the SIGN of the returned handle (ok = rc > 0, main.c:810). The pt_call FAILURE branch (main.c:280-283) would require a lost SIGTRAP or non-SIGTRAP stop - neither exists in the evidence (module_start_return stamped in 4/4 boots).

Post-pt_call cleanup is BYTE-IDENTICAL for OK and FAIL: kernel_mprotect de-exec (main.c:448), pt_munmap (452), notify OK/FAIL - only the string differs (812 vs 814), restore_creds (816), pt_detach (817), all_ok=0 (819, no break - the loop CONTINUES to the next plugin; only death-while-waiting breaks, main.c:787). There is NO cleanup timeout and NO cleanup retry anywhere in the file.
wait_for_needs is charged PER PLUGIN (main.c:784, inside the per-plugin loop): path_test re-pays the full readiness wait ~0.8s after composition already passed it.

wait_stable (main.c:518-559): tick=50ms; max_ticks = max_ms/tick = 500 for mode 2 (25000/50). There is NO clock check inside the loop: max_ms bounds the TICK COUNT, not wall time. The loop's only sleep is usleep(50ms) per tick (554).

Per-tick compute: count_modules (main.c:531 -> 492-499) = 128 kernel_dynlib_mapbase_addr calls, called a FIRST time at 531; deps_ready (538 -> 509-514) = 3x(dynlib_handle+mapbase) + pt_resolve <=2 + count_modules' 128 again = ~136. Total ~264 kernel calls per tick, none short-circuited for a healthy game process (all deps present).

wait_stable exits: (a) fast path - 20 consecutive stable-count ticks (stable_req=20, main.c:521) + usleep(600ms) settle + re-verify (540-545); (b) exhaust path - 500 ticks then 'try anyway if still alive' returns 1 (557-558). Both paths return 1; neither records which path ran.
pt_attach (main.c:176-190): <=3 attempts x (kill(0) + PT_ATTACH + waitpid_timeout(2000) + usleep(300ms)) = <=6.9s worst; typically 1 attempt ~0.3s.

pt_syscall (main.c:214-250, used by pt_mmap/pt_munmap at 252-258): PT_STEP loop capped at 10000 iterations, each paying waitpid_timeout(pid,NULL,1000) (WNOHANG poll every 10ms) + PT_GETREGS; breaks when rsp unwinds past entry (2-4 steps for a syscall stub).

Remaining inter-plugin calls are ms-class: notify = 1 sceKernelSendNotificationRequest (main.c:128-140); restore_creds = 10 kernel_copyin + 2 kernel sets (321-346); jb_pid = 9 copyin + 2 sets (349-376); save_creds = 10 copyout + 2 gets (294-319); pt_detach = 1 ptrace with 2 ucred authid switches (145-157, 192-194).

worst_case_arithmetic.note: sleep-only worst case (the model that produced 'the ~32s worst case'):
worst_case_arithmetic.answer_to_mission: The ~32s worst case is the SLEEP-ONLY bound of the ONE path both plugins take regardless of failure or success (F03/F04: there is no distinct failure-path flow). The latency worker's '~2-3s' was the same path's fast case (fast readiness 1.6s sleep-only + typical attach). Neither figure modeled F06/F07: the tick loop's kernel-call compute is unbounded by max_ms, and the readiness burn happens TWICE per invocation (F05).
worst_case_arithmetic.wall_clock_model: gap = cleanup(0.05-0.5) + readiness(20x(0.05+264K)+0.6 fast | 500x(0.05+264K) full-burn) + attach(0.3-6.9) + creds(~0) + inject-to-stamp(0.2-0.5), where K = per-kernel-call seconds
worst_case_arithmetic.h1_fit: full-burn with K~0.30-0.33ms: 500x(0.05+264*0.0003)=64.6s + 0.3 + 0.3-6.9 + 0.3 = 65.5-72.2s -> matches all four boots (70.7-71.8s) with ONE stable parameter; run1's +0.9s is attach/jitter-class

hypotheses.text: path_test's readiness re-payment (F05) runs its FULL 500-tick burn (module count never holds 20 stable ticks mid-boot) and the tick compute (~264 kernel calls x 500 ticks = 132,000 calls at K~0.3ms) stretches the '25s' budget to ~64s wall (F06/F07)
hypotheses.why: deterministic across 4 boots (fixed tick cap, stable K); only hypothesis whose fitted parameter lands in a plausible range; explains why composition's own pre-module_start readiness is invisible-but-large

hypotheses.text: pt_syscall step-loop pathology (F10) walking thousands of instructions
hypotheses.why: no mechanism for ~3500 clean steps through a 2-3 instruction munmap stub; would also inflate composition's own inject_prx dt. DISCRIMINATOR for next run: composition FAIL toast dt ~1-2s (H1) vs ~70s (H2); patch 03 steplog records it durably

hypotheses.text: pt_call's 30s waitpid timeout fired on composition (lost SIGTRAP), then readiness
hypotheses.why: module_start_return stamped +802ms in 4/4 boots (SIGTRAP demonstrably generated); predicted totals 40.6s (fast readiness) or >=88s (full burn with same K) - neither is 70.9s

hypotheses.text: second ploader invocation, or 3+ ini entries between composition and path_test (missing files each paying readiness)
hypotheses.why: ini law is the 2-plugin 1216aab6 config (verified in LAUNCH-DAY-10 pre-state, staging never writes the ini); ploader is one-shot per launch

hypotheses.text: mission's primary hypothesis: a failed-plugin cleanup timeout
hypotheses.why: F03/F04: the failure path is the success path plus one toast string; no cleanup timeout, no retry, no extra wait exists on rc<=0

fix_estimate.02_hoist_readiness_existing: removes the per-plugin re-payment (the dominant term): gap 70.9s -> 0.8-7.9s (cleanup 0.3-0.5 + attach 0.3-6.9 + inject-to-stamp 0.2-0.5); saves ~63-70s of MEASURED gap per invocation
fix_estimate.05_wallclock_deadline_new: bounds ANY readiness wait to max_ms WALL: full-burn capped at ~25.3s instead of ~64s; total mod-side serial <= ~34s worst with 02, vs implied ~137s today; zero behavior change in the fast path (500 ticks already take >=25s of sleep alone)
fix_estimate.05_alone: gap <= ~32.7s (saves ~38s when settling; 0 when stable); does NOT fix the double payment

ini_order_mitigation_verdict: REJECTED: moving path_test first would make PATH_TEST stamp BEFORE composition's refusal - it masks the measured gap, saves ZERO real seconds (both readiness burns are still paid; total serial unchanged), breaks the documented terminator guard (LAUNCH-DAY-10: 'PATH_TEST stamps prove full ini traversal (path_test is the TERMINATOR)'), and loses comparability with runs 1-4.
honesty: The 70.7-71.8s gap is MEASURED (4/4 boots, per-writer same-clock stamps). Its INTERNAL split (readiness vs attach vs cleanup) is INFERENCE from pinned source: no ploader-side stamps exist in any log; patch 03 (steplog) is the instrument that will confirm or refute H1's split.
K (~0.3ms per kernel_dynlib call) is a FITTED parameter, not an independent measurement; no datum for it exists in the evidence. The whole H1 attribution stands or falls with it - flagged as such.

Composition's OWN readiness burn (before module_start_entered, outside the measured gap) is inferred by symmetry with H1 and is unmeasured; this EXTENDS the implied injection age beyond TIMING T07's '~2-28s' bound, which had silently assumed sleep-only readiness.
The mission's run4 stamps were re-derived from raw evidence, not trusted: refusal [t=62842697ms pid=370] and PATH_TEST 62913653732826ns reproduce exactly (gap 70.957s).

Patch 05 is verified to apply (patch -p1, zero offsets/rejects) both standalone and after the 01-04 series; full compilation requires PS5 SDK headers, unavailable on this host - same verification standard as the latency worker's series.
